facts.quote: Curbside pickup is available at all of our branches . Cold Spring, Carrico/Fort Thomas & Newport Sunday 1 – 5 pm Monday – Thursday 9 am – 9 pm Friday 9 am – 7 pm Saturday 9 am – 5 pm Alexandria Sunday 1 – 5 pm Monday – Friday 9 am – 7 pm Saturday 9 am – 5 pm Requesting Items Books, audiobooks, DVDs, CDs, video games and magazines may be checked out through this service. Log into your library account . You can call or email us if you need help accessing your account or placing a hold. Search for an item in our catalog and click "Request Item" to place it on hold. Wait for a phone call, text, email or postal mail notifying you that your holds are ready for pickup. Follow instructions for curbside pickup below. Picking Up Items You will be notified by phone, text, email or postal mail when your holds are available for curbside pickup. Please note that your holds are not ready for pickup until you receive a notification and the items are marked as "Held" in your account. Once you are notified that your holds are available, drive to your designated branch during curbside pickup hours. Park in one of the parking spots that are designated for curbside pickup. Let us know that you are outside by calling the number listed on the parking spot's sign. We will need your name, library card number and parking spot number. If a staff member doesn't answer, do not leave a voicemail message. Please call back until a staff member answers. Remain in your vehicle. A staff member will place your items directly in your vehicle, preferably into your trunk.
facts.text: Curbside pickup is available at Cold Spring. Wait for your hold-ready notification, park in a designated curbside space and call the number on its sign with your name, library card number and parking space number. Stay in your vehicle for staff delivery.

facts.quote: Q: Who can use curbside pickup? A: Curbside pickup is available for current physical library card holders. The service is not available for digital library card holders. Q: How long will I have to pick up my holds once I have been notified that they are ready? A: You will have seven days to pick up your holds. Q: What if the parking spots designated for curbside pickup are full? A: If the parking spots are full, please park in another area of the parking lot until one is available. We will only deliver items to vehicles parked in the designated spots. Q: Who can pick up my items? A: Anyone may pick up your items. They must have your library card number in order to do so. Staff will not release items to those without a library card number.
facts.text: Curbside pickup requires a current physical library card; a digital-only card does not qualify. Holds are kept for seven days after notification. Someone else can collect them with your library card number.

facts.quote: The Campbell County Public Library Outreach Department offers a variety of services to give homebound residents of Campbell County access to the library's resources. Read about some of our Adult Outreach services below. If you'd like to set up one of these services, call our Adult Outreach Services Assistant at 859-572-5035, ext. 352. Book Talks Our Adult Outreach Services Assistant is available to host monthly book talks at senior centers, adult day care facilities, retirement living homes and extended care facilities. This service differs from a book club in that no particular book is selected to be read by each participant. Instead, topics of interest vary and a presentation is given to educate attendees and encourage intellectually stimulating discussion. Deposit Collections Deposit collections are books loaned to nursing homes, senior centers and other community agencies throughout Campbell County. Collections of 20-30 items are specially selected for each site. Deposit collections may contain an assortment of large print and regular print books, magazines, audiobooks, CDs and DVDs. These collections are delivered on a rotating schedule every four weeks, depending on the facility's needs. Home Delivery Service If you are a resident of Campbell County and cannot visit the library because of temporary or permanent illness or disability, you are eligible for our home delivery service. Materials available for delivery include regular print books, large print books, magazines, DVDs, audiobooks and CDs. Materials are selected based on your reading interests and needs. The Adult Outreach Services Assistant will deliver the materials to your home on a specified day. You may also sign up to have your materials delivered by mail for free.
facts.text: The library system offers home delivery for Campbell County residents who cannot visit because of a temporary or permanent illness or disability. Materials can also be mailed for free. To arrange the service, call Adult Outreach at 859-572-5035, ext. 352.

To obtain a physical card, the library asks for photo ID and proof of current address, with an application completed at a branch. Applications are available in Spanish. Discuss any difficulty providing documents with the library before travelling.
facts.quote: All you need is a valid photo ID and proof of your current address to get a library card with CCPL! Stop by one of our branches to complete a library card application. Applications are available in Spanish.

facts.text: Digital Patron Cards provide online materials, but do not permit physical borrowing or use of library computers. Contact a branch to verify your local address before using Kentucky Libraries Unbound. Digital cards need annual renewal; questions can go to digitalaccess@cc-pl.org.
facts.quote: Digital Patron Cards must be renewed annually. Contact digitalaccess@cc-pl.org with questions concerning your Digital Patron Card.

facts.text: The card page announces that beginning January 3, 2027, Hamilton and Clermont County, Ohio residents will be offered a free Easy Access Card limited to three physical items at a time, library computers and online databases. It separately says out-of-state residents who work in Campbell County can keep free full access with proof of employment. Confirm the card type before relying on a future pickup.
facts.quote: The Campbell County Public Library will end reciprocity for free full access library cards to those living outside the state of Kentucky. We will continue to offer free full access library cards to those living outside the state but who work in Campbell County (proof will be required). Beginning January 3, 2027, for residents of Hamilton and Clermont Counties in Ohio, we will offer an Easy Access Card for free. Easy Access Cards provide the cardholder the ability to checkout up to three physical items (two books and one non-book item checked out at a time), log onto library computers and access our online databases.

additionalSupport.quote: After verifying your local address by contacting one of our branches, you can download eBooks and audiobooks on Kentucky Libraries Unbound.
